chunks.arabic_text: صَالِحُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ عَطِيَّةً، الْأَضْخَمُ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ، بَصْرِيٌّ. كَانَ أَخْبَارِيًّا. وَهُوَ ضَعِيفٌ.

translations.en: Salih ibn Ali ibn Atiyyah, al-Adkham (the corpulent), Abu Muhammad, Basran. He was a traditionist (akhbari). He is weak.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* characterizes Salih ibn Ali as an 'akhbari,' a term in Shia scholarship often denoting a narrator who relies heavily on transmitted reports (akhbar) but may lack rigorous analytical scrutiny (ra'y) or precise memory. His designation as 'weak' (da'if) highlights the critical importance Shia scholars place on the balance between narrative transmission and intellectual precision in establishing reliable hadith chains. This evaluation serves as a cautionary note for jurists relying on his narrations for legal derivation.
en.seo_question: Who is Salih ibn Ali al-Adkham and what is his status in hadith sciences?

key_terms.أخباريا: A traditionist, one who relies heavily on narrations (akhbar) rather than deep reasoning (ra'y).
key_terms.ضعيف: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator is not considered fully reliable.
key_terms.الأضخم: The corpulent or fat, a descriptive nickname (laqab) used to distinguish this narrator.
